Let \(V=\operatorname{Sym}_3(\mathbb F_3)\). Since every symmetric matrix over \(\mathbb F_3\) diagonalizes by congruence, a rank \(r\) symmetric matrix is a sum of \(r\) rank-one symmetric matrices, and not fewer by rank subadditivity. Hence

\[
d(A,B)=\operatorname{rank}(A-B).
\]

So this is a translation-invariant metric on the additive group \(V\).

For a character indexed by \(Y\in V\), write

\[
\widehat f(Y)=\sum_{X\in V} \operatorname{rank}(X)^p\,\chi_Y(X).
\]

The \(p\)-negative type condition is equivalent to

\[
\widehat f(Y)\le 0\qquad \text{for every }Y\ne0.
\]

A direct finite Fourier count by congruence class of \(Y\) gives the nontrivial eigenvalues, with \(a=2^p\), \(b=3^p\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{type of }Y & \widehat f(Y)\\ \hline
\operatorname{rank}Y=1 & -1+18a-18b\\
\operatorname{rank}Y=2,\ \text{anisotropic} & -10+27a-18b\\
\operatorname{rank}Y=2,\ \text{hyperbolic} & 8+9a-18b\\
\operatorname{rank}Y=3 & -1-9a+9b
\end{array}
\]

The first three remain negative up to the critical point. The last one is increasing and vanishes exactly when

\[
-1-9\cdot 2^p+9\cdot 3^p=0,
\]

i.e.

\[
3^p-2^p=\frac19.
\]

Thus \(\wp\) is the unique positive real number \(\rho\) satisfying

\[
3^\rho-2^\rho=\frac19.
\]

At \(p=\rho\), equality occurs exactly on the full-rank nonzero Fourier characters. The number of nonsingular symmetric \(3\times3\) matrices over \(\mathbb F_3\) is \(468\), so

\[
\dim E=468.
\]

\[
\boxed{(\wp,\dim E)=\left(\rho,468\right),\quad 3^\rho-2^\rho=\frac19}
\]
